correctness.rationale: A chain-increasing partial injection equals a unique pair of equally long increasing subsequences. Parity and two-sided fence adjacency force initial equal parity and each paired gap of type (1,1), even-even ≥2 or odd-odd ≥3, exactly as the source Proposition 1. Summing initial-pair, arbitrary gap sequence and two endpoint slacks gives the bivariate rational kernel; symmetric diagonal extraction gives A(z)=((1-z²)/sqrt(1−2z−3z²+4z³+4z⁶)−1)/z (branch with constant one). Factoring radicand as (1+z)(1−2z²)(1−3z+2z²−2z³) isolates the unique smallest positive singularity rho=0.396608..., and square-root transfer yields C rho^-n n^-1/2. Independent definition-level enumeration of every valid increasing map for n=0..8 matches the first nine coefficients, and independent symbolic generating-series expansion checks its finite expansion. These tests support normalization but not the asymptotic proof.
residual_risks: The normalized rank refined coefficient [x^n y^n] is mathematical rank of partial maps, distinct from generator rank.
No full census beyond checked finite n; asymptotic relies on analytic singularity proof.
